Sparse functional principal components of growth trajectories

Source: R/pheno.R
wgh_fpca.Rd

Summarises each child's z-score trajectory with functional principal component scores (PACE, fdapace), which work with sparse and irregular visits. Children must meet a minimum number of visits and follow-up span.

Usage

wgh_fpca(
  x,
  outcome = "haz",
  age_range = c(5, 18),
  min_visits = 4,
  min_span = 3,
  max_k = 4,
  fve = 0.95
)

Arguments

x

Growth data.

outcome

Trajectory variable (default "haz").

age_range

Ages used.

min_visits, min_span

Eligibility. Ho (2026, medRxiv 2026.09.05.26362315) required 4 visits over 3 years.

max_k

Maximum number of components.

fve

Fraction of variance explained used to choose the number of components.

Value

A list of class wgh_fpca with scores (one row per child), fit, fve and the mean function.

Examples

# \donttest{
fp <- wgh_fpca(growdat2_mini[growdat2_mini$sex == "Male", ], age_range = c(5, 18))
head(fp$scores)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   id      sex    fpc1    fpc2    fpc3
#>   <chr>   <fct> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 C000044 Male   1.22  0.235   0.330 
#> 2 C000118 Male   1.27  0.0985  0.610 
#> 3 C000169 Male   2.82  0.0168  0.137 
#> 4 C000344 Male   2.32  0.699   0.204 
#> 5 C000362 Male   2.79 -0.0685  0.881 
#> 6 C000428 Male   2.95  0.435  -0.0863
# }
